newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's SABIC lifts first half net profit 1.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's SABIC lifts first half net profit 1.3 pct.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said on Monday it lifted net profit 1.3 percent in the first half of 1997 to 2.30 billion riyals ($613.3 million).
SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, made a 2.27 billion riyal net profit in the first six months of 1996.
Figures released by the Riyadh-based company said it sold various products worth 11.90 billion riyals between January and end-June 1997, up from 9.94 billion a year earlier.
SABIC, which accounts for around five percent of the world's petrochemical output, produces mainly petrochemicals, fertilisers, plastics and steel.

It has embarked on an ambitious programme to raise its annual production capacity to 28 million tonnes by the year 2000 from around 23 million now. SABIC controls and operates 16 production complexes with Japanese and Western companies.
Shareholders' equity at end-June 1997 climbed to 27.41 billion riyals from 25.74 billion and total assets grew to 63.61 billion riyals from 60.55 billion.
